title: Ordinary signed-total quotient tensor maps and invertible target computations
statement: Let R,S be commutative condensed rings, a:R→S a monoid morphism, and f:X→Y an arbitrary scheme morphism. Use internal module derived categories and the actual D,L, scalar and pullback counits of [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons], and the scalar tensor normalization of [lem-sfb-quotient-section-tensor-normalization]. Define pullComplex and scalarComplex by applying ordinary pullback and extension termwise. Define totalPull and totalScalar by the signed direct-sum total tensorators, and totalBalance by prolonging pullIso(a,f).inv. Define ordinaryLeft(P,Q) = totalBalance(P tensor Q) then scalarComplex_X(totalPull(P,Q)) then totalScalar_X(f*P,f*Q); define ordinaryRight(P,Q) = pullComplex_S(totalScalar_Y(P,Q)) then totalPull_S(aP,aQ) then totalBalance(P) tensor totalBalance(Q). These maps agree for all integer-indexed complexes P,Q, without flatness. Define factorCompute(P) = D_X(computePull(P)) then compute_X(f*P), targetCompute(P,Q) as the tensor of these factor maps, sourceCompute(P,Q) = L_S D_Y(mu_Q(P,Q)) then L_S(compute_Y(P tensor Q)) then computePull(a(P tensor Q)), and targetLocalization(P,Q) = mu_Q(a(f*P),a(f*Q)). For the invertibility assertions, assume the section R-module category on every scheme admits the recorded derived category. Then targetCompute is invertible when P,Q are K-flat. If P,Q also have flat terms and bX is a TensorNormalized scalar tensor iso at X, targetLocalization is invertible. Under this last invertibility assumption define targetTensor as its inverse.

proof.text: Use the already proved scalarPull_monoidal ordinary calculation: extension/restriction and geometric pull/push are monoidal adjunctions, and comapLowerStarIso is monoidal. Its conjugate pullIso.inv is monoidal. Functor.mapHomologicalComplexδNatTrans_naturality, expanded by mapHomologicalComplexδNatTrans_comp on both composites, proves ordinaryLeft=ordinaryRight on signed direct-sum totals. The ordinary helper is defined before, and does not use, the exact scalar-extension hypotheses in its source module. The totalPull definition selects the canonical monoidal_upperStar projection explicitly, rather than relying on inference through the reducible composite functor.

Geometric pullback preserves K-flat complexes and has an invertible computation counit. Scalar computation is invertible at the pulled-back K-flat complexes. Their tensors give invertibility of targetCompute. For targetLocalization use TensorNormalized at the pulled-back flat-term K-flat pair: its right side is an isomorphism, since tensoring preserves K-flatness and the scalar and ordinary tensor computation maps are invertible. The other two factors on the left are isomorphisms, so targetLocalization is an isomorphism. All maps are explicit constructions.
